prompt: What is Cloud Run's default maximum number of concurrent requests per instance?
Twenty requests, each waiting 200 ms, took 4.07 s one at a time and 0.61 s twenty at once. Why?

choices.text: Docker started extra containers for the burst
choices.why: One container served every request.

choices.text: The delay is skipped when requests arrive together
choices.why: Each request still waited; they waited together.

choices.text: Waits overlap on threads; they do not add up
choices.why: Right. Waiting is what threads share for free.

choices.text: The laptop gave the container more CPUs
choices.why: Nothing changed the container's CPU.

prompt: In the run of 200 requests, 80 at a time, the median was 0.209 s and the slowest 2.062 s. What does the lesson read in that gap?
hint: Which became the limit, the wait or the program?

choices.text: 80 is above what this program carries
choices.why: Right. Its connection queue overflowed and clients retried.

choices.text: The database stand-in slowed down under load
choices.why: The delay is a fixed sleep.

choices.text: The laptop ran out of memory
choices.why: Nothing points at memory.

choices.text: Cloud Run would cap the burst at 20
choices.why: Nothing ran on Cloud Run.

prompt: A service renders a PDF per request, using a full vCPU for a second. With concurrency 80 on 1 vCPU, what happens under load?

choices.text: Cloud Run starts a new instance when CPU reaches 100%
choices.why: It starts one when requests reach the concurrency.

choices.text: Each request gets its own vCPU automatically
choices.why: Concurrency shares the instance's CPU.

choices.text: Requests beyond the first are refused with 429
choices.why: They are accepted, up to 80.

choices.text: One vCPU is shared, and latency climbs
choices.why: Right. Lower the concurrency for work that computes.

prompt: Python's http.server keeps a queue of connections waiting to be accepted, ___ by default.
With the default CPU allocation, what does an instance get between requests?

choices.text: A full vCPU, billed at the idle rate
choices.why: The idle rate is for minimum instances, and the CPU is throttled.

choices.text: Almost no CPU
choices.why: Right. It answers the next request at once, but cannot work in between.

choices.text: Nothing: it is shut down after each request
choices.why: It stays alive, just throttled.

choices.text: Half a vCPU, to finish background work
choices.why: There is no such allowance.

prompt: From runcost.py, what does instance-based billing cost a month for 1 vCPU and 512 MiB, in USD?
hint: The same at every busy share.

prompt: Request-based, busy 25% of the month: active vCPU 0.000024 and memory 0.0000025 per second, 1 vCPU and 0.5 GiB, 2,628,000 seconds. What is the cost in USD?
A service answers at once and then sends a confirmation email in a background thread. With the default CPU allocation, what happens to the email?
hint: Who has the CPU after the response?

choices.text: It is sent normally, a few milliseconds later
choices.why: The CPU was taken away with the response.

choices.text: Cloud Run refuses to start background threads
choices.why: Threads start; they just get no CPU.

choices.text: It is late or lost; it belongs in a queue
choices.why: Right. Lesson 20's Cloud Tasks, or a job.

choices.text: It is sent and billed at the request rate
choices.why: Not reliably sent at all.

prompt: A service is busy 90% of the time. By runcost.py's arithmetic, which billing is cheaper, and why?
hint: Where do the two lines cross?

choices.text: Instance-based: past about 75% busy, its lower rate wins
choices.why: Right. 49.93 flat against about 60 by request.

choices.text: Request-based, because it never charges for idle time
choices.why: At 90% busy there is little idle time to save.

choices.text: They cost the same at any busy share
choices.why: Only instance-based is flat.

choices.text: Request-based, because of its free tier of two million requests
choices.why: The free tier is small next to a month at 90%.

prompt: Instance-based billing is set with cpu____ = false in Terraform.
Which part of a cold start is entirely yours to shorten?

choices.text: Fetching the image from Artifact Registry
choices.why: Cloud Run streams it; it is mostly the platform's.

choices.text: Setting up the sandbox around the container
choices.why: That is the platform's.

choices.text: The time the request spends on the internet
choices.why: That is not part of the cold start.

choices.text: What the program does before it listens
choices.why: Right. Imports, connections, caches.

prompt: On this laptop, how many seconds did it take from docker run to the first answer from /health? Answer to two decimals.
Importing the Pub/Sub client took 0.38 s with Python's start; the orders service's imports took 0.05 s. What follows for a service on Cloud Run?
hint: Each instance pays it once, at start.

choices.text: Every request is 0.33 s slower with the big library
choices.why: Imports happen once per instance, not per request.

choices.text: Each cold start pays the import, so defer heavy ones
choices.why: Right. Import a rare dependency where it is used.

choices.text: Cloud Run caches imports between instances
choices.why: Each instance is a fresh process.

choices.text: The difference vanishes on Cloud Run's faster machines
choices.why: Nothing measured here says so.

prompt: Put the parts of a cold start in the order they happen.
trap: Listening is the last step: nothing is routed to the instance until it happens.

prompt: Why does the course quote no cold-start time for Cloud Run itself?

choices.text: Cloud Run has no cold starts with min instances
choices.why: Minimums hide them; they still exist.

choices.text: Google forbids publishing timings
choices.why: That is not the reason.

choices.text: None of these timings came from Cloud Run
choices.why: Right. Nothing is invented.

choices.text: Cold starts on Cloud Run are always under 10 ms
choices.why: No such guarantee exists.

prompt: A minimum instance of 1 vCPU and 0.5 GiB is idle 95% of a 2,628,000-second month at 0.0000025 per vCPU-second and per GiB-second. What does the idle time cost, in USD?
Which service gains most from min_instance_count = 1?
hint: Who meets a cold start most often?

choices.text: One called a few times hourly
choices.why: Right. Almost every call would start cold.

choices.text: One with steady traffic all day
choices.why: An instance is always running there anyway.

choices.text: A job that runs at night
choices.why: Jobs have no minimum instances.

choices.text: One that has never been called
choices.why: Then nobody would notice the start.

prompt: A service splits traffic 90/10 between two revisions and has min_instance_count = 1. How many warm instances can that keep?
hint: A minimum is per revision with traffic.

choices.text: One, shared by both revisions
choices.why: Each revision with traffic keeps its own.

choices.text: None until the split is 100/0
choices.why: Splits do not disable minimums.

choices.text: Ten, the maximum
choices.why: The maximum is a ceiling.

choices.text: Two, one per revision with traffic
choices.why: Right. Both are billed while idle.

prompt: What does startup_cpu_boost do?

choices.text: Keeps a CPU warm between requests
choices.why: That is cpu_idle = false.

choices.text: Gives extra CPU while the instance starts
choices.why: Right. Then it is taken away.

choices.text: Doubles the CPU for every request
choices.why: Only at start, and for a short while.

choices.text: Starts a spare instance before it is needed
choices.why: That is a minimum instance.

prompt: Put the lesson's four decisions in the order it recommends.
items: CPU allocation, from the busy share
A shorter start, in the program
A minimum and a boost, for what is left
trap: A minimum first pays every month to hide what a shorter start would remove.

prompt: Match each symptom to the setting that addresses it.

pairs.left: Latency climbs on one instance doing CPU work
Background work after the response never finishes
pairs.right: Move it to a queue or a job

pairs.left: The first call of the morning is slow
Busy 90% of the time and costly

prompt: A team sets concurrency to 1 "to be safe" on a service that waits on a database. Under a burst of 50 simultaneous requests, what changes?

choices.text: Nothing: Cloud Run queues the 49 others on one instance
choices.why: It starts more instances instead.

choices.text: Requests are faster, since each has a whole instance
choices.why: They wait on the database either way, and some wait for a start.

choices.text: Up to 50 instances start, many cold, each billed
choices.why: Right. The default would carry it on one.

choices.text: The database receives fewer connections
choices.why: Fifty instances open at least as many.

prompt: Request-based billing rounds each billed stretch up to how many milliseconds?
Which of these did this lesson measure on the laptop? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: How long a container took to answer its first request
choices.why: Right; about half a second.

choices.text: What importing the Pub/Sub client costs
choices.why: Right; 0.38 s with Python's start.

choices.text: How long Cloud Run takes to pull the image
choices.why: Nothing here runs on Cloud Run.

choices.text: How much startup CPU boost speeds up a start
choices.why: The lab cannot measure it and quotes no gain.
